subject: Next steps & POC kickoff — scope, data owners, and success metrics (Mavenlytics)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
To: Liam Torres <liam.t@mavenlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@mavenlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & POC kickoff — scope, data owners, and success metrics (Mavenlytics)

Thanks again for the slot today — good conversation and a clear set of priorities. I wanted to capture what we heard and propose a tight POC kickoff plan so we can align owners and unblock access.

Recap of main pains you shared
- Inconsistent entity extraction across customer documents (in particular: invoices and SLA PDFs).
- Latency and cost spikes when running batch inference on historic data.
- Lack of reliable evals to track quality regressions after model changes.

High-level POC goal
- Demonstrate a production-configured Redwood inference pipeline that reduces inference cost per document by ~35% while improving extraction F1 by 8-12% on your invoice dataset.

Proposed scope (30-day pilot)
- Dataset: 5k labeled invoices + 20k unlabeled historical invoices for throughput/cost testing.
- Models: start with open-model baseline (Llama-variant) + quantized variant; we’ll run a small eval suite on both.
- Integration: S3 drop + event-driven inference via your staging account.

Success metrics (measured end of pilot)
- Extraction F1 on labeled test set >= baseline + 8% (primary).
- Median generation latency under 350ms per document for typical sizes (SLO).
- Token cost reduction >= 30% via batching/caching/quantization (economic target).

Owners and roles
- Mavenlytics: Liam T. (Data & access owner), Priya S. (Security/Procurement).
- Redwood: Rafael M. (Eng + PM lead), Marissa C. (Onboarding/ops), Soojin L. (evals + prompt matrix).

Immediate access/setup asks
1) Provide staging S3 bucket ARN and an initial sample (up to 500 invoices) by Oct 6.
2) A short CSV listing data owners and contact info (see attached data-owners-matrix.xlsx).
3) Confirm whether Mavenlytics wants SSO (SAML) for Redwood Console access — if yes, security team contact appreciated.

Planned kickoff cadence
- Week 0 (this week): data drop + access validated.
- Week 1: baseline evals + quick wins (prompt tweaks, batching config).
- Week 2–3: throughput tuning, caching, quantized runs.
- Week 4: acceptance evals, cost analysis, and next-steps decision.

Prompt set & eval plan (brief)
- We'll run a 3-tier prompt matrix: (1) strict extraction, (2) contextual inference, (3) fallback heuristics.
- Evals: unit-level F1, end-to-end extraction accuracy, and human review on 200 random docs.

Attachments
- poc-charter-v1.pdf (POC scope + timeline + roles)
- data-owners-matrix.xlsx (template)

Ask: Can you confirm dataset availability and your preferred kickoff window next week? If Wednesday/Thursday morning PT works, we’ll lock a 60-min technical kickoff and invite your security contact for a 15-min intro.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[r] redwood.com
From: Liam Torres <liam.t@mavenlytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mavenlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & POC kickoff — scope, data owners, and success metrics (Mavenlytics)

Rafael — thanks for the clear summary and the charter. Quick answers from our side:

- We can provision the staging S3 and drop an initial sample of ~400 invoices by Tue (Oct 6).
- Data owners matrix: I’ll fill the sheet and include contacts for our security person (security@mavenlytics.com).
- SSO: yes, we prefer SAML SSO for console access; I’ll loop in Priya to coordinate.

A couple of clarifying questions before the kickoff:
1) For the 5k labeled set, does Redwood need a specific label schema, or can we map our current fields? We currently annotate: invoice_number, vendor_name, total_amount, due_date, line_items (semi-structured).
2) For the latency SLO: is the 350ms target measured from our event ingestion to model output, or just model-serving time? We need to understand how end-to-end measurements will be reported for our SLA review.

We’re happy to do Wed 10/7 09:30 PT for the 60-min kickoff — will that work for you and the team? Priya — can you confirm if security will join the first 15?

—Liam
Liam Torres
Head of Data Platforms, Mavenlytics
liam.t@mavenlytics.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
To: Liam Torres <liam.t@mavenlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@mavenlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps & POC kickoff — scope, data owners, and success metrics (Mavenlytics)

Thanks Liam — Wed 10/7 09:30 PT is confirmed on our side. Calendar invite and technical agenda incoming (sending now).

Quick answers inline: 
- Label schema: we can accept your existing fields. Soojin will share a short mapping template before the kickoff to ensure our eval scripts align with your schema (no rework on your end).
- Latency SLO: the 350ms target is model-serving median (model inference + network hop inside the Redwoods runtime). For end-to-end (event ingestion -> downstream), we’ll provide both model-served and end-to-end reports; SLA language for contracts can reference the model-served SLO and a separate operational objective for end-to-end.

Action items before Wed kickoff (owners):
- Mavenlytics (Liam): S3 sample drop (<=500 docs) and completed data-owners matrix by Tue EOD (Oct 6).
- Mavenlytics (Priya): security contact and SSO preference / metadata by Tue EOD.
- Redwood (Marissa): onboarding runbook & temporary console accounts (will send invite).
- Redwood (Soojin): eval mapping template + initial prompt matrix (will share before meeting).

Attachments: poc-charter-v1.pdf (attached)

If anything blocks the S3 drop, flag it here and we’ll provision an alternate upload link. Looking forward to kicking off.

Best,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
